title: Ultrastrong coupling of topologically protected edge and bulk magnetoplasmons without a dedicated cavity
authors: F. Velli, P. Sai, M. Dub, J. Dzian, F. Le Mardele, M. Mittendorff, M. Orlita, W. Knap, C. Lange
abstract: In the ultrastrong light-matter coupling regime, the ability to confine the electric field to subwavelength scales and define an electromagnetic mode is essential. This task is typically achieved through dedicated cavities, such as THz metal resonators. Here, we instead introduce ultrastrong coupling directly between distinct magnetoplasmon excitations, leveraging solely the spatial symmetry of a confined electronic medium in the presence of a magnetic field. By patterning an AlGaN/GaN single quantum well hosting a two-dimensional electron gas into micrometer-scale patches, we tailor the mutual interactions between topologically protected edge and bulk magnetoplasmons, achieving coupling strengths of up to 0.1. The progressive breaking of rotational symmetry determines the coupling rules and leads to the emergence of energy gaps and unique chiral-mode hybridization. Our results highlight a path towards exploiting the symmetry class and topology of the magnetoplasmon wavefunction as a new parameter space for ultrastrong light-matter interaction without a dedicated cavity.
summary: This paper demonstrates how to achieve ultrastrong coupling between magnetoplasmon modes in patterned semiconductor nanostructures, eliminating the need for external resonant cavities. By controlling the geometry and symmetry of the electron gas, researchers can engineer strong, tunable interactions between topologically protected edge and bulk plasmon modes. This opens a new parameter space for quantum light-matter interaction based on material topology.
main_problem: The research aims to achieve ultrastrong light-matter coupling between magnetoplasmon excitations without relying on conventional dedicated electromagnetic cavities.
main_result: By patterning the semiconductor material geometry (e.g., square or rectangular patches), the coupling strength can be engineered up to 0.1, leading to observable energy gaps and chiral-mode hybridization.
method: The study combines experimental magnetospectroscopy on patterned AlGaN/GaN quantum wells with theoretical modeling using quantum Hamiltonians and Finite-Element Method (FEM) simulations.
model_or_system: The system is a two-dimensional electron gas (2DEG) in patterned AlGaN/GaN quantum wells subjected to a perpendicular magnetic field. The physics is described by a quantum Hamiltonian incorporating magnetoplasmon modes and coupling terms.
key_observables: Magnetoplasmon-Polariton (MPP) doublet splitting, energy gaps at zero magnetic field, and the magnetic field dependence of the plasmon resonance frequency.
important_parameters: Ultrastrong coupling regime ($\Omega_R/\omega_0 \approx 0.1$), magnetic field strength (up to 16 T), and the geometric symmetry (disk $	o$ square $	o$ rectangle).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the ability to tailor interactions solely through the spatial symmetry of the confined medium, bypassing cavity-related field distortions.
figures_summary: Figures show SEM images of patterned patches (disk, square, rectangle) and corresponding magnetospectroscopy results illustrating the anti-crossing and mode hybridization.
paper_structure: The work progresses by first establishing the physical platform and the need to bypass cavities, then developing the quantum model and Hamiltonian, and finally demonstrating the control over coupling and mode hybridization by systematically changing the geometry's symmetry.
why_interesting: This work provides a novel, purely material-based method to engineer strong light-matter coupling, which is a central theme in cavity QED and quantum optics, by leveraging topological and symmetry properties of plasmons.
